biography: Alexander "Flash" Sims, a name synonymous with audacious overtakes and blonde bravado, hails from the quiet English countryside, a stark contrast to the roaring racetracks he now commands. His foray into motorsport began, not with a silver spoon, but with a beat-up kart his father salvaged from a local scrapyard. He spent his teenage years tearing up the local karting scene, developing a fearless, almost reckless, driving style that quickly earned him both admirers and detractors. A defining moment came at the 2007 Formula Renault UK Winter Series, where a daring last-lap maneuver, squeezing past two rivals at Paddock Hill Bend, secured him the championship and caught the eye of BMW Motorsport. Now a seasoned veteran with BMW M8 GTE, Sims continues to chase podiums, though whispers of retirement occasionally surface amidst the tyre smoke and champagne showers.
drivingStyle: Sims is a driver who lives on the edge. His driving style can be described as aggressive and instinctive. He's known for late braking maneuvers and squeezing every last ounce of performance from his car. While this approach has yielded spectacular results, it also makes him prone to errors and tire wear, especially in longer races. Tire management isn't his forte; instead, he prefers to push hard and rely on his raw speed to compensate, making him a thrilling, if somewhat unpredictable, driver to watch.
rivalries: Marco Rossi: A long-standing feud originating from a controversial collision during the 2018 Spa 24 Hours, where Rossi accused Sims of reckless driving.
Isabelle Dubois: A clash of personalities and driving styles; Dubois, known for her calculated approach, often criticizes Sims' aggressive tactics.
Kenji Tanaka: A rivalry fueled by a shared ambition for the top spot in the GT racing world; their battles on track are always intense and closely contested.
quirks: Always wears a lucky blue wristband given to him by his grandmother before every race.
Listens to classical music to calm his nerves before a race.
Refuses to use the number 13 on his car, considering it bad luck.
careerHighlight: Winning the 2019 24 Hours of Daytona with BMW M8 GTE. It was a hard-fought victory against formidable competition, showcasing his resilience and skill under pressure.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the 2020 24 Hours of Le Mans. A mechanical failure led to a spectacular crash, costing him a potential victory and leaving him devastated.
